Mechanical formatting qualification

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-hardening-submission-cleanup-formatting-readme.Rmd
contributor-tools-hardening-submission-cleanup-formatting-readme.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

These receipts bind the formatting phase to source commit 01bb39ccf8373ae8965a2679ee4813a63ea2d85d. No R/man source is modified by the proof runner. source-manifest.json checks 98 package source/documentation files before and after reproduction. Later evidence-only commits may change HEAD; the source hashes remain the acceptance condition.

The before snapshots are the parent’s helper-decomposition state immediately before this formatting phase. They are not the originally submitted package. The submitted-source BiocCheck comparison is a separate qualification.

Executed proofs

  • 35 R files: 19 raw parse ASTs identical; 16 equivalent after the explicit constant-string/local-binding normalizations in scope.json and prove.R. No numerical expression, native call argument, control flow or RNG call is changed by these normalizations.
  • 38 split literals retain their exact evaluated character text. Actual conditionMessage() output also matches for signal arguments.
  • Parsed roxygen semantics match in all 35 files. Parameter-name groups are expanded before comparison: the one overlong internal group was split into two groups with the same description for each original parameter.
  • All 11 new long generated-wrapper lines reproduce byte for byte from the before snapshot; their raw R ASTs and native argument order are identical.
  • rd-only regeneration wrote only prepare_execution.Rd, joining a standalone “or” onto the preceding description line. No examples or APIs changed.

R/s4_count_store.R is excluded from the 35-file AST/documentation comparison because the parent subsequently extracted an axis-label validator to keep its validity function below the new function-length threshold. Its three literal splits are included in the text manifest; the later structural change has a separate semantic review. The four migration/distributed-owner R files were not edited by this agent. See scope.json for the precise boundaries.

No check exclusions or suppressions were added. Existing inherited long lines are not relabeled as new coverage or silently removed. The original-checker baseline gate is recorded separately by the parent task.

Reproduce

From any directory, with base R, Python, roxygen2, pkgload, jsonlite and the package’s development dependencies available:

bash tools/hardening/submission-cleanup/formatting/run-proof.sh /path/to/sceptre

The runner extracts compact before/after snapshots into a temporary directory, verifies current source hashes, reproduces the AST and parsed-documentation CSVs, checks signal text, and reproduces the generated binding formatting. It then verifies source hashes again. The full terminal result is in reproduction.log; normalizations are inspectable rather than implicit.

When intentionally regenerating native bindings later, the associated step is:

Rcpp::compileAttributes(".")
python3 tools/hardening/submission-cleanup/formatting/wrap-generated-bindings.py R/RcppExports.R

The formatter touches only the named new wrappers when they exceed 80 columns. It does not run compileAttributes, rewrite C++, reorder arguments, or alter inherited generated wrappers. The regeneration command was not run during this phase because native interfaces were unchanged.

For documentation, use the current source namespace without native compilation:

roxygen2::roxygenise(".", roclets = "rd", load_code = function(path) {
    pkgload::load_all(path, compile = FALSE, helpers = FALSE,
                     attach_testthat = FALSE, recompile = FALSE)$env
})

Only generated files with changed bytes should enter the source diff. The recorded successful regeneration used the same source-loading approach with compile = FALSE; its log is retained. Full package tests and original-version BiocCheck qualification are separate from these mechanical proofs.
